recipes.title: Oyster Sauce Lettuce
recipes.description: Lettuce leaves blanched for seconds and topped with a hot garlic and oyster sauce dressing.

steps.instructionText: Wash the lettuce and discard any damaged leaves.
Put 1 litre of cold water in a pot with 3 ml of the oil and half the salt, and bring it to a boil.
Blanch the lettuce leaf by leaf, each for 10 seconds. Drain well and arrange on a plate.
In a bowl, mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, remaining salt and the sugar with 15 ml of cold water.
Heat the remaining oil in a wok, add the garlic and fry until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce, bring it to a boil and turn off the heat at once. Pour it evenly over the lettuce.

recipes.title: Stir-fried Bok Choy
recipes.description: Bok choy stir-fried with garlic, then briefly braised with a pinch of sugar.

steps.instructionText: Separate the bok choy into leaves and wash them well.
Mince the garlic.
Heat the wok over medium-high heat and add the oil. Wait 30 seconds for the oil to get hot.
Add the bok choy and stir-fry for about 1 minute, until it softens.
Add the garlic and stir.
Pour in the water so it almost covers the greens, add the salt and stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Add the sugar, cover and cook over low heat for 2 minutes, then serve.

recipes.title: Tiger Skin Peppers
recipes.description: Long green peppers pressed in hot garlic oil until blistered, then tossed in a sweet-sour soy sauce.

steps.instructionText: Cut off the pepper stems and rinse the peppers under the tap.
Cut each pepper lengthways into 3-4 long pieces.
Peel the garlic and chop it finely. Put the oil in a small bowl and stir in the garlic.
In another bowl, mix the sugar, soy sauce, vinegar and salt.
Pour the garlic oil into the wok and heat it to about 150 °C. Add the peppers in a single layer, not overlapping.
Keep pressing the peppers with the spatula, turning them over now and then.
Stir-fry for about 2 minutes, until the skins blister and wrinkle, then pour in the sauce.
Turn up the heat, stir-fry for 30 seconds and serve.

recipes.title: Zucchini and Egg Stir-fry
recipes.description: Soft zucchini and fluffy scrambled egg, stir-fried with a little tomato.

steps.instructionText: Wash the tomato and cut it into small pieces.
Wash the zucchini and cut it into diamonds about 4 cm across.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well.
Heat the wok and add 10 ml of the oil. Pour in the eggs and stir-fry until set. Break them into small pieces with the spatula and move them to a bowl.
Add the remaining oil and the tomato and stir-fry until soft.
Add the zucchini and toss well. Add the salt, turn the heat down and cook for 4-5 minutes.
Return the eggs and stir-fry over medium heat for 15 seconds. Turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Spinach and Egg Stir-fry
recipes.description: Blanched spinach tossed over high heat with pieces of golden egg.

steps.instructionText: Trim the roots off the spinach, wash it, put it in a sieve and blanch it in boiling water. Drain.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well.
Heat the wok and add 10 ml of the oil.
When the oil is hot, pour in the eggs and cook over medium heat for 15 seconds to set into a pancake, then cut it into small pieces with the spatula.
Turn off the heat and move the egg to a plate. Do not wash the wok.
Turn the heat back on and add the remaining oil. When hot, add the spinach and stir-fry over high heat for 15 seconds, then add the egg and toss.
Add the salt and 100 ml of drinking water and stir-fry over high heat for 10 seconds. Turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Egg Custard
recipes.description: Silky savoury egg custard steamed until it wobbles like jelly, finished with soy sauce and sesame oil.

steps.instructionText: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the salt and beat well.
Add the vinegar if using; it takes away the eggy smell.
Stir in the warm water, 1 to 1.5 times the volume of the egg. Less water gives a firmer custard, more water a softer one.
Strain the egg mixture to remove the foam, so the custard is smooth. Cover the bowl with a lid, an upturned plate or cling film.
Bring 300-500 ml of water to a boil in a pot, then put the covered bowl in.
Steam over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 more minutes.
Shake the bowl: the custard is done when it is no longer liquid and wobbles like jelly.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and soy sauce and serve.

recipes.title: Pan-fried Scallion Tofu
recipes.description: Golden pan-fried tofu slices tossed with green chilli and finished with scallion.

ingredients.name: cooking oil, plus a little extra

steps.instructionText: Rinse the tofu, cut it into slices about 5 mm thick and lay them on a plate.
Wash the scallion, trim the root and chop it.
Wash the chilli, split it, remove the seeds and cut it into 1 cm squares.
Heat the wok and add the 18 ml of oil, swirling it over the base.
Lay in the tofu and fry over low heat until golden underneath, then turn. When both sides are golden, move it to a plate.
Add a little more oil to cover the base. Add the chilli and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes, pressing it with the spatula.
Return the tofu, add the salt and bouillon powder and stir-fry over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add 10 ml of water and let it cook off over high heat. Sprinkle with the scallion and serve.

recipes.title: Crispy Tofu with Soy Glaze
recipes.description: Egg-coated tofu slices fried golden, then simmered in a sweet soy and oyster sauce glaze.

steps.instructionText: Beat the eggs in a bowl.
For the sauce, mix the light soy sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, 10 g of the cornstarch and the water.
Cut the tofu into 10 slices about 1.2 cm thick.
Spread the remaining cornstarch on a plate. Coat each tofu slice in cornstarch, then dip it in the egg.
Heat a frying pan, add the oil and wait 10 seconds for it to heat up.
Lay the tofu in the pan in one layer and fry over low heat until golden, then turn.
When both sides are golden, pour in the sauce so every piece sits in it. Cook over high heat for 3 minutes until thick.
Turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Cold Tofu Salad
recipes.description: Briefly boiled tofu cubes dressed with soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil and scallion.

steps.instructionText: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Bring 500 ml of drinking water to a boil over high heat.
Boil the tofu for 1-2 minutes to remove the beany taste and firm it up.
Lift out the tofu, drain well and put it in a bowl.
Wash the scallion and chop it. Peel and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, sugar and garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the sauce over the tofu and sprinkle with the scallion.
Drizzle with the chilli oil if you like, then toss gently and serve.

recipes.title: Braised Ash Gourd (Winter Melon)
recipes.description: Golden-fried ash gourd cubes braised soft in soy and oyster sauce, with a glossy sauce.

steps.instructionText: Peel the ash gourd and cut it into cubes no bigger than 2 cm.
Heat the oil in a wok, add the ash gourd and fry gently, turning, for 2 minutes until the surface is golden.
Lift the ash gourd into a large bowl, leaving the oil in the wok.
Fry the ginger, light soy sauce and oyster sauce in the remaining oil for 15 seconds.
Return the ash gourd and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in boiling water to just cover the ash gourd and boil over high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the dark soy sauce for colour and keep cooking until the ash gourd is soft and a chopstick goes in easily.
Add the bouillon powder, rice wine and scallion, stir-fry for 30 seconds, then lift the ash gourd into a bowl.
Mix the cornstarch with a little water. Stir it into the liquid left in the wok, bring to a boil and pour over the ash gourd.

recipes.title: Salt and Pepper Corn
recipes.description: Starch-coated sweetcorn fried crisp and tossed with Sichuan pepper salt and sesame seeds.

steps.instructionText: Thaw the corn by soaking it in warm water for 15 minutes (or boiling it for 5 minutes). Drain.
Spread the corn in a sieve or tray lined with paper towels and shake until the paper is soaked.
Move the corn to a second lined tray and shake again. Repeat until no water drops are visible but the corn is still slightly moist.
Add the cornstarch, enough to cover the corn, and shake until every kernel is coated.
Heat a wok and add enough oil to cover the base, but not much more. Heat it until very hot (about 200 °C), then add the corn.
Fry over medium heat for 30 seconds without stirring, so the coating stays on.
Stir gently for 3 minutes, then take the corn out.
Sprinkle with the pepper salt and sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.title: Candied Potatoes (Basi Tudou)
recipes.description: Fried potato chunks coated in hot caramel that pulls into threads, topped with sesame.

steps.instructionText: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small even chunks. Toss them in the dry cornstarch until coated.
Heat the oil in a wok, add the potatoes and fry, turning gently, for 5-7 minutes until a chopstick goes in easily.
Lift the potatoes into a large bowl. Pour the oil out of the wok and keep it for other cooking.
Put the water and sugar in the wok. Stir slowly in one direction until the syrup turns brown.
Return the potatoes and toss for 30 seconds to coat them, then plate.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.title: Cabbage, Egg and Glass Noodles
recipes.description: Shredded cabbage and carrot stir-fried with soft glass noodles, scrambled egg and soy sauces.

steps.instructionText: Cut the carrot and cabbage into thin strips.
Soak the glass noodles in cold water for 1 hour.
Put the noodles into boiling water until soft, then drain.
Beat the eggs with 1 g of the salt for 15 seconds.
Chop the spring onion, garlic and dried chillies into small pieces.
Heat half the oil in a wok, add the eggs and scramble until cooked. Take them out.
Add the remaining oil and fry the spring onion, garlic and chillies for 8 seconds.
Add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the glass noodles, the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and remaining salt and toss well.
Return the eggs and stir-fry for about 15 seconds, then serve.

recipes.title: Golden Coin Eggs
recipes.description: Hunan-style boiled egg slices pan-fried golden with chillies, garlic and bean paste.

steps.instructionText: Put the eggs in cold water, bring to a boil over high heat, then cook over low heat for 8 minutes.
Cool the eggs under running water so they peel easily, then peel them.
Mince the garlic finely. Chop the long green chilli and bird's eye chillies into 2-3 mm pieces.
Cut each egg crossways into 4 round slices of similar size.
If using cornstarch, coat each egg slice and shake off the excess.
Heat 25 ml of the oil in a pan (20 ml if not using cornstarch) and add the egg slices.
When lightly browned underneath, add the remaining 10 ml of oil and turn the slices.
When the second side is golden, add the chillies and garlic and fry for about 1 minute, then turn the slices.
Add the doubanjiang, fry for about 30 seconds and turn the slices again.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar, pour it over the eggs, toss the pan gently and serve.

recipes.title: Silky Scrambled Eggs
recipes.description: Soft, barely set Cantonese-style scrambled eggs made creamy with a splash of milk.

steps.instructionText: Beat the eggs with the milk and 5 ml of the oil until evenly mixed.
Heat a frying pan over high heat for 30 seconds, then add the remaining oil.
Heat for 30 seconds more, then turn the heat to low and pour in the eggs.
Leave for 5 seconds, then slowly push the egg from the edges towards the centre with the spatula.
When the eggs are mostly set, turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Garlic Stir-fried Celery
recipes.description: Crunchy celery flashed over high heat with garlic for just 30 seconds.

steps.instructionText: Pick off most of the celery leaves, keeping a few tender ones. Split thick stalks lengthways, then cut into pieces no longer than 5 cm.
Mince the garlic.
Drain the celery and shake it as dry as you can.
Heat the wok and add the lard. When hot, sprinkle in the salt.
Add the garlic and fry over low heat for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Turn the heat to high, add the celery and stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds. Serve at once, while it is bright green and crisp.

recipes.title: Sweetcorn with Pine Nuts
recipes.description: Sweetcorn and carrot in a light sweet glaze, finished with toasted pine nuts.

steps.instructionText: Blanch the corn and carrot in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat the wok, add the oil and stir-fry the carrot briefly, then add the corn and stir-fry.
Add the sugar and salt and toss well.
Mix the cornstarch with the water, pour it in and stir quickly until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the pine nuts, toss and serve.

recipes.title: Stir-fried Lotus Root
recipes.description: Crisp lotus root cubes stir-fried with spring onion, chilli and soy and oyster sauces.

steps.instructionText: Cut the spring onion and chillies into short pieces.
Peel the lotus root and cut it into pieces no bigger than 3 cm. Keep them in water so they do not darken.
Bring 500 ml of water to a boil in a wok. Blanch the lotus root for 2 minutes, then lift it onto a plate.
Pour out the water and heat the wok until dry. Add the oil.
When the oil is hot, fry the spring onion and chillies until fragrant.
Add the lotus root and stir-fry over high heat.
Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and oyster sauce, stir-fry for 2 minutes and serve.

recipes.title: Qianlong Cabbage Salad
recipes.description: Beijing cold dish of hand-torn napa cabbage in a tangy sesame paste and vinegar dressing.

steps.instructionText: Use only the tender yellow inner leaves of the cabbage. Tear them by hand into pieces about half the size of your palm; do not cut them.
Rinse the leaves and drain them very well, or the dressing will not cling.
Put the sesame paste in a bowl. Add the vinegar and stir in one direction until it thins and falls in a thin ribbon.
Stir in the sugar, then the salt, then the sesame oil, mixing well after each.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage and toss gently by hand until every leaf is coated.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve, or leave for 5 minutes first to let the flavours soak in.

recipes.title: Hunan Sour and Spicy Eggs
recipes.description: Eggs fried in hot oil and broken up, then tossed with garlic, chilli and a black vinegar sauce.

steps.instructionText: Crack the eggs into a bowl without beating them.
Cut the scallion into 3 cm lengths. Crush the garlic and chillies to a paste (a garlic press works well).
In a small bowl, mix the vinegar, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and a splash of water to make the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok until hot and pour in the eggs. When they set, break them into large pieces with the spatula.
Add the garlic and chilli paste and pour in the sauce.
Let the sauce reduce over high heat. Just before serving, add the scallion.

recipes.title: Fish-fragrant Aubergine
recipes.description: Sichuan fried aubergine with a little pork in a sweet, sour and spicy bean paste sauce (no fish).

steps.instructionText: Cut the aubergines into strips. Chop the scallion, keeping the white and green parts apart. Chop the ginger and garlic and dice the chilli.
For the sauce, mix the salt, MSG, sugar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar and cornstarch slurry in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over low heat until very hot and just smoking, about 40 seconds.
Fry the aubergine for 2 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden. Lift it out and pour off the oil, leaving about 20 ml in the wok.
Stir-fry the pork until it turns white, then take it out.
Add 20 ml of the frying oil. Fry the doubanjiang, scallion whites, ginger, garlic and chilli until fragrant, then return the pork and stir.
Add 100 ml of water, the aubergine and the sauce. Stir-fry over high heat until the sauce thickens and coats the aubergine.
Stir in the scallion greens and serve.

recipes.title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
recipes.description: Loaded egg fried rice with prawns, luncheon meat, peas, carrot and corn.

steps.instructionText: Dice the carrot and luncheon meat into very small cubes (about 2 mm). Chop the scallion, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Beat the eggs in a bowl.
Boil the carrot, peas and corn until cooked and lift them out. Cook the prawns in the same water, then drain.
Heat the wok, add 25 ml of the oil and heat it. Pour in the egg in a thin stream and do not stir.
As soon as the egg sets, lift it out.
Stir-fry the luncheon meat, peas, carrot, corn and prawns for 1-2 minutes, then set aside.
Rinse the wok so it is clean; a little oil can stay.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the scallion whites until fragrant.
Turn the heat to low, add the rice and press and toss it with the spatula until every grain is coated in oil and separate.
Add the egg and keep pressing so it breaks up and mixes into the rice.
Turn the heat to high, add the other cooked ingredients and stir-fry quickly for 1-2 minutes. Add the salt and toss well.
Add the scallion greens, stir-fry for 1 minute and serve.

recipes.title: Scallion Oil Noodles
recipes.description: Shanghai noodles tossed in slowly fried scallion oil with soy sauce and sugar.

steps.instructionText: Wash the scallions and cut them into 5-7 cm lengths, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Fry the scallion whites until lightly golden.
Add the scallion greens and turn the heat to low.
Keep frying gently for 15-20 minutes, until the scallions are dark golden and crisp. Lift them out, leaving the oil in the wok.
Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar to the oil. Stir over low heat for about 1 minute until the sugar dissolves, then turn off the heat.
Pour the sauce into a jar. You need 30 ml now; the rest keeps in the sealed jar once cool.
Bring 2 litres of water to a boil. Cook the noodles until done, usually 3-8 minutes (check the packet).
Drain the noodles and divide them between two bowls.
Add 15 ml of the scallion oil sauce to each bowl, top with some fried scallions if you like, and mix well.

recipes.title: Tomato and Egg Noodles
recipes.description: Noodles tossed in a quick tomato, egg and capsicum sauce.

steps.instructionText: Chop the scallion, keeping the white and green parts apart. Mince the garlic. Cut the tomato into chunks and the capsicum into diamonds.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl, adding the vinegar if they smell eggy.
Heat the wok and add the oil. When hot, pour in the eggs and scramble until fully set. Move them to a bowl, leaving some oil in the wok.
Fry the scallion whites and garlic until fragrant. Add the tomato and capsicum and cook until the tomato releases some juice.
Add the soy sauce and sugar and stir-fry for 10 seconds. Pour in just enough water to almost cover the tomato.
When it boils, add the eggs, oyster sauce and salt. Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the scallion greens and sesame oil and move the sauce to a serving bowl.
Without washing the wok, bring 500 ml of water to a boil and add the noodles. When they soften, add 100 ml of cold water.
When it boils again and the noodles float, add another 100 ml of water.
When it boils once more and the noodles look translucent, lift them into the sauce bowl and mix.

recipes.title: Shaanxi Oil-splashed Noodles
recipes.description: Thick wheat noodles and greens topped with chilli flakes, garlic and scallion, then doused in smoking oil.

steps.instructionText: If using hand-pulled noodle strips, press each lightly with a rolling pin, hold both ends and gently pull it longer.
Chop the scallion and mince the garlic. Wash the greens and bean sprouts.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat and add 1 g of the salt.
Add the noodles and stir gently so they do not stick. When they float, cook for 1-2 minutes more, adding the greens and bean sprouts for the last minute.
Drain the noodles, greens and sprouts and put them in a large bowl.
Top with the soy sauce, vinegar, scallion, garlic, chilli flakes and remaining salt.
Heat the oil in a pan until very hot and just smoking. Pour it evenly over the chilli flakes; it should sizzle.
Mix the noodles and toppings well with chopsticks and serve.

recipes.title: Stir-fried Instant Noodles
recipes.description: Instant noodles briefly boiled, then stir-fried with egg, sausage and their own seasoning.

steps.instructionText: Cut the ham sausage into 1 cm pieces.
Bring 1200 ml of water to a full boil. Add the noodle block and cook for 45 seconds, loosening the noodles, then turn off the heat. Do not cook them through.
Scoop out 80 ml of the hot noodle water and keep it. Drain the noodles, rinse briefly in cold water and drain well.
Squeeze all the vegetable and sauce sachets and half to most of the seasoning powder into a small bowl. Stir in the 80 ml of noodle water.
Beat the egg in a bowl, without salt.
Heat the wok, add 8 ml of the oil and pour in the egg. Stir-fry for about 20 seconds until set, then take it out.
Reheat the wok and add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the sausage for 10 seconds.
Add the noodles and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the sauce from the bowl and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return the egg, stir-fry for 30 seconds more and serve.

recipes.title: Shou Zhua Bing (Flaky Pancake)
recipes.description: Layered, crisp pan-fried flatbread rolled up with egg, lettuce, ham and cheese.

steps.instructionText: Put the flour in a bowl and stir in the boiling water until shaggy. Add the cold water and knead into a smooth dough. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into pieces of about 100 g, shape them into balls and roll each one out thinly.
Brush with oil and sprinkle with salt. Roll each sheet up and coil it like a snail shell. Rest for 10 minutes.
Roll each coil out again into an even, thin pancake.
Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the pancakes over low heat until golden and puffed on both sides.
Fry the egg. Top the pancakes with the egg, lettuce, ham and cheese, roll them up and serve.

recipes.title: Ants Climbing a Tree
recipes.description: Sichuan glass noodles simmered with minced pork in chilli bean paste until they soak up the sauce.

steps.instructionText: Soak the glass noodles in water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain.
Finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Heat the wok, add the oil and fry the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry until it turns pale and releases a little fat.
Add the doubanjiang and fry until the oil turns red.
Add the light and dark soy sauce and stir well.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and stir gently with chopsticks so they do not stick.
Simmer over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes, until the noodles have soaked up the liquid and look almost dry.
Sprinkle with chopped scallion if you like, turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Pan-fried Frozen Dumplings
recipes.description: Frozen dumplings steamed and then fried in one pan until crisp and golden underneath.

steps.instructionText: Put the oil in a frying pan (non-stick is best), turn on the heat and add the dumplings in one layer, not stacked.
Straight away, pour in water to come halfway up the dumplings.
Cover and cook over high heat for 8-10 minutes.
When only about 2 mm of water is left, turn the heat to medium and let them fry.
When the water has gone, shake the pan so the dumplings brown evenly.
Scatter over the sesame seeds and scallion, cover and cook for 10 seconds.
After 1-2 minutes, lift one dumpling to check. When the bottom is golden and crisp, take them out at once.

recipes.title: Millet Congee
recipes.description: Northern Chinese foxtail millet porridge, simmered until creamy.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the millet once in a bowl of water, swirling it by hand, and pour the water off. Do not rub the grains.
Bring the water to a full boil.
Pour the millet into the boiling water and stir so it does not stick to the bottom.
Boil over high heat for 6-10 minutes, stirring a few times.
Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15-20 minutes with the lid slightly open, stirring now and then so it does not catch.

recipes.title: Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup
recipes.description: Light soup of soaked laver seaweed with ribbons of egg, scallion and sesame oil.

steps.instructionText: Soak the seaweed in water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Beat the eggs.
Put the water, oil and salt in a pot and bring to a boil. Add the seaweed.
Boil the seaweed for 3 minutes.
Slowly pour in the egg in a thin stream and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the scallion and cook over low heat for 20 seconds.
Turn off the heat, add a few drops of sesame oil and serve.

recipes.title: Tomato, Egg and Tofu Soup
recipes.description: Quick tomato broth with soft tofu and egg, lightly thickened with cornstarch.

steps.instructionText: Dice the tomatoes, beat the eggs in a bowl and cut the tofu into cubes. Mix the cornstarch with a little cold water.
Heat the oil in a pot, add the ginger and after 5 seconds add the tomatoes. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the boiling water. When it boils again, wait 60 seconds, then add the egg and tofu.
When the soup returns to the boil, add the cornstarch mixture and stir twice in one direction.
Add the bouillon powder, salt and scallion, cook for 30 seconds and serve.

recipes.title: Corn and Pork Rib Soup
recipes.description: Clear pork rib soup slow-simmered with sweetcorn and carrot.

steps.instructionText: Cut the leek into 3-4 cm lengths and bruise them with the back of a knife. Cut the corn into small pieces and the carrot into chunks. Peel the ginger and cut it into large slices.
Chop the ribs into small pieces.
Put the ribs in cold water with the leek, half the ginger and the rice wine. Bring to a boil over high heat, skim off the scum, then drain the ribs.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the ribs with the remaining ginger until lightly browned. Add the vinegar and fry for 1 more minute.
Pour in all the boiling water at once (do not add more later) and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the corn and black pepper, cover and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes.
Add the carrot, cover and simmer for 40 minutes more.
Stir in the salt and simmer for 3 minutes more. Sprinkle with the spring onion and serve.

recipes.title: Tea Eggs
recipes.description: Boiled eggs with cracked shells simmered in black tea, soy sauce and whole spices.

steps.instructionText: Put the eggs in cold water and boil them over high heat for about 8 minutes.
Lift out the eggs and cool them in cold water.
Tap the eggs against each other until every shell is cracked.
Return the eggs to the pot with the star anise, bay leaves, cinnamon, fennel seeds, rock sugar, black tea, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and salt.
Add water to cover the eggs. Bring to a boil over high heat, then simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove the tea and spices. For a deeper flavour, leave the eggs to soak in the liquid a while longer.

recipes.title: Oat and Egg Pancake
recipes.description: Quick breakfast pancake of oats, milk and egg, with optional greens.

ingredients.name: chopped greens such as spinach, optional

steps.instructionText: Mix about 80 ml of the milk with the oats until thick.
Beat the eggs until evenly yellow.
Pour the eggs into the oat mixture and stir until thick and even.
Melt a thin layer of butter in a frying pan, spreading it over the base.
Pour in the batter and spread it into a round pancake.
Cook over low heat for 2-3 minutes. If using the greens, scatter them on while it cooks.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes more.
Serve with the rest of the milk to drink.

recipes.title: Yang Zhi Gan Lu (Mango Chia)
recipes.description: Hong Kong mango dessert drink made with chia seeds, grapefruit and coconut milk.

steps.instructionText: Soak the chia seeds in the milk for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel half the mango and the grapefruit, dice them and put them in a tall glass.
Cut the other half of the mango into chunks and blend with the ice cubes and coconut milk until smooth.
Add the soaked chia seeds to the glass and pour in the mango mixture. Top with the dried mango and orange, if using.

recipes.title: Winter Melon Tea
recipes.description: Ash gourd slowly cooked down with rock sugar into a sweet concentrate to dilute and drink.

steps.instructionText: Peel the ash gourd, remove the seeds and cut it into pieces no bigger than 4 cm.
Mix in the rock sugar, cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
The ash gourd will have released lots of liquid. Tip everything into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 1-2 hours, stirring often so it does not catch.
Strain through a sieve. Discard the ash gourd and keep the liquid.
Let it cool, pour it into a clean container and refrigerate.
This is a concentrate: dilute it with water to taste and serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Fried Milk (Zha Xian Nai)
recipes.description: Chilled sweet milk custard cut into sticks, crumbed and fried until crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.instructionText: Mix 80 ml of the milk with the cornstarch until no lumps remain.
Put the remaining 170 ml of milk and the sugar in a pan and stir over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again and pour it slowly into the pan, stirring all the time.
Keep stirring over low heat for 3-5 minutes, until thick enough that a line drawn across the base holds for 3 seconds.
Brush a 20 x 15 cm heatproof dish with about 2 ml of the oil. Pour in the mixture and smooth it to about 2 cm thick.
Cool to room temperature, cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until firm and not sticky to the touch.
Turn it out and cut it into 12 sticks of about 6 x 2 x 2 cm.
Put the flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in three dishes. Coat each stick in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil over medium heat to 165-175 °C. Without a thermometer, a few breadcrumbs should float within 2 seconds and keep bubbling.
Fry in 2-3 batches for 60-90 seconds each, turning once or twice.
When evenly golden, lift out and drain on kitchen paper for about 2 minutes before eating.

recipes.title: Sugar-frosted Taro (Arbi)
recipes.description: Chaoshan snack of fried taro sticks tossed in hot syrup until the sugar turns white and frosty.

steps.instructionText: Peel the taro and cut it into fairly thick sticks so they do not break when tossed.
Heat enough oil to cover the taro until small bubbles form around a chopstick dipped in it.
Fry the taro until it floats, turns pale golden and a chopstick goes in easily. Lift it out (keep the oil for other cooking).
In a clean pan, heat the sugar and water until full of small bubbles but not yet coloured.
Add the scallion and taro, turn off the heat and keep tossing. As it cools, the sugar turns white and frosty on the taro.
Serve.

recipes.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.description: Sichuan chicken cubes with peanuts, toasted dried chillies and Sichuan pepper in a light sweet-sour sauce.

steps.instructionText: Debone the chicken leg with scissors (skip this for chicken breast). Pound the meat with the back of a knife and cut it into 1.5 cm cubes. Soak in water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Put the spring onion greens and the ginger in a bowl and pour over 50 ml of boiling water. Cut the spring onion whites into 1.5 cm pieces.
Microwave the peanuts on high for 5 minutes to dry them out.
Mix the chicken with the salt, dark soy sauce, rice wine and 15 g of the cornstarch. Slowly mix in some of the spring onion water until sticky.
Cover the chicken and marinate in the fridge for 1 hour.
Cut the chillies into short pieces. Heat the wok, turn it to low and toast the chillies until slightly charred, then the Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant. Set aside.
Turn the heat to high and add the oil. When hot, add the chicken. Fry until the top turns white, then turn it, fry for 30 seconds and stir-fry.
Add the spring onion whites. Top up the leftover spring onion water to 100 ml with hot water, pour it in, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to high. Add the peanuts, chillies, Sichuan peppercorns, bouillon powder, vinegar and sugar and toss well.
Mix the remaining 10 g of cornstarch with 50 ml of water, stir it in and cook until the sauce is as thick as you like.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve.

recipes.title: Fish-fragrant Shredded Pork
recipes.description: Sichuan pork strips with carrot, capsicum and wood ear in a sweet, sour and spicy sauce (no fish).

steps.instructionText: Soak the wood ear mushrooms for 4 hours, rinse and cut them into small pieces.
Cut the pork into thin strips. Mix 5 ml of the soy sauce, the rice wine, 5 g of the cornstarch, 20 ml of the water and the egg white, add the pork and marinate for 15-30 minutes.
For the sauce, mix the remaining soy sauce, the vinegar, sugar, salt, remaining cornstarch and remaining water.
Seed the capsicum and cut it into strips. Cut the carrot into strips and blanch it in boiling water.
Mince the ginger and garlic. Cut the scallion into 5 mm pieces.
Heat the wok, add 15 ml of the oil and quickly stir-fry the pork until it turns pale. Take it out.
Heat the remaining oil and add the scallion, ginger, garlic and doubanjiang.
Add the carrot and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add the capsicum and wood ear and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the pork and toss quickly, for no more than 20 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss for no more than 15 seconds. Turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Cola Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Pan-fried chicken wings simmered in cola and soy sauce until sticky and glossy.

steps.instructionText: Put the wings in a pot, cover with cold water and add 1 slice of ginger and the rice wine. Bring to a boil over high heat (about 2 minutes), skim off the scum and drain. Skip this for fresh wings.
Cut two slashes into each side of every wing. Marinate the wings in 10 g of the light soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Heat a little oil over low heat and fry the remaining ginger until fragrant. Add the wings and fry until golden on both sides, stirring a few times so nothing sticks.
Pour in cola to cover the wings and bring to a boil over high heat. Skim off the dark foam and add the scallion knot.
Season with the salt, sugar, remaining light soy sauce and the dark soy sauce for colour.
When the scallion knot turns yellow, remove it with the ginger. Keep simmering over medium heat.
When the cola turns syrupy and clings to the wings, turn the heat to low so the glaze coats them, then serve.

recipes.title: Hunan Red-braised Pork
recipes.description: Pork belly cubes caramelised in rock sugar and slowly braised with spices and soy sauce.

steps.instructionText: Wash the pork belly, put it in cold water with 2 slices of the ginger and bring to a boil. Lift it out and rinse off the scum under cold water.
Cut the pork into 1.5 cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a wok, add the rock sugar and stir over low heat until it turns caramel brown. Add the pork and stir-fry over medium heat until coloured.
Add the remaining ginger, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice wine, dried chillies and salt. Stir-fry over low heat for 1 minute.
Pour in boiling water to cover the pork. Cover and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Turn the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes so it does not stick.
When about a third of the liquid is left, turn the heat to medium and reduce the sauce until thick, then serve.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs
recipes.description: Blanched and fried pork ribs glazed in a sweet, tangy sauce with sesame seeds.

steps.instructionText: Put the ribs and ginger in cold water and bring to a boil over high heat. When lots of foam appears, turn the heat down and blanch for 2-3 minutes. Drain.
Rinse the ribs 2-3 times with boiling water to remove all the scum.
Heat the oil to about 170 °C and fry the ribs for 3-5 minutes until lightly golden. Drain.
In a clean wok over low heat, warm 50 ml of hot water, add the sugar and stir gently until dissolved and pale yellow.
Add the ribs and stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds.
Add the vinegar, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, bouillon powder, ketchup and five-spice powder and stir-fry for 30 seconds to coat.
Pour in boiling water to just cover the ribs and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the dark soy sauce for colour and reduce the sauce quickly.
If the ribs are large, cover and simmer over low heat for 5-10 minutes so they absorb the flavour.
Plate the ribs and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Hunan Chilli Pork Stir-fry
recipes.description: Thin pork belly slices stir-fried with fresh red chillies, fermented black beans and bean paste.

steps.instructionText: Slice the pork belly thinly. Mix it with the cornstarch, dark soy sauce and salt and marinate for 30 minutes.
Cut the scallion into lengths. Slice the red chillies and bird's eye chillies diagonally.
Heat the wok and add the oil. When hot, stir-fry the pork until it changes colour, then take it out.
Fry the garlic in the wok until fragrant, add the douchi and stir well.
Add the doubanjiang and stir well.
Return the pork and stir-fry to mix.
Add all the chillies and the scallion, stir-fry for 40 seconds and serve.

recipes.title: Huangmen Braised Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken pieces caramelised, then braised with shiitake, dried chilli and green pepper.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the dried shiitake and soak them overnight. Keep the soaking water and slice the mushrooms.
Wash the chicken legs and chop them into 4 cm pieces.
Slice the ginger and cut the chillies into rings. Cut the green peppers into long strips and the potato, if using, into chunks the size of the chicken.
Put a little oil and the sugar in a cold wok. Heat slowly over low heat, stirring all the time, until the sugar melts and turns deep brown.
Quickly add the chicken, turn the heat to high and stir-fry fast. Splash in the rice wine and stir-fry briefly.
Add the ginger and dried chillies, then the soy sauce, and stir well.
Pour in the mushroom water (or plain water) to cover the chicken. Add the mushrooms, white pepper, salt and potato.
Stir, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes.
When the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick but not dry, add the green peppers.
Add the MSG, toss well and turn off the heat while the peppers are still crisp.

recipes.title: Scallion-braised Chicken
recipes.description: Boneless chicken leg seared crisp, then braised briefly with leek, spring onion and soy sauce.

steps.instructionText: Debone the chicken legs with scissors: cut along the bone from the thick end, snip the meat free and pull the bone out.
Cut the meat into 2-3 cm pieces. Cut the leek into 0.5 cm slices and the spring onions into 1 cm lengths.
Mix the chicken with the rice wine, 5 ml of the light soy sauce, the salt and white pepper and marinate for 10 minutes.
For the sauce, mix the remaining light soy sauce, the dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok. Fry the ginger and Sichuan peppercorns over low heat until the ginger browns, then scoop them out and discard.
Over medium-high heat, spread out the chicken and leave it for 2-3 minutes to form a golden crust underneath.
Stir-fry until all sides have changed colour and the chicken is cooked through.
Add the leek and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce, toss well, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Uncover, add the spring onions and sesame seeds, toss for 5-10 seconds and serve.

recipes.title: Shredded Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Poached chicken breast torn into shreds and dressed with Sichuan pepper oil, soy sauce and vinegar.

steps.instructionText: Slice the ginger.
Put 4 litres of water in a pot with the chicken breast, ginger and rice wine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, uncovered. Turn to medium heat and skim off the foam.
Cook for 5-7 minutes more: 5 for fresh chicken, 7 for frozen. It is done when a chopstick goes in easily; cook longer if needed.
Rinse the chicken in cooled boiled water until it is at room temperature.
Tear the chicken into thin shreds along the grain.
In a bowl, stir the Sichuan pepper oil, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and salt until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour the dressing over the chicken, mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Cantonese Steamed Sea Bass
recipes.description: Whole sea bass steamed with ginger and scallion, dressed with soy sauce and sizzling oil.

steps.instructionText: Slice the ginger, then cut it into thin shreds. Cut the scallion whites into lengths and the greens into fine shreds. Soak the shreds in cold water.
Rinse the fish and pat it dry. Score both sides a few times. Rub the salt over the fish inside and out to clean off the slime, then leave for at least 10 minutes.
Stuff half the ginger and scallion whites into the belly and scatter the rest over the fish. Put the fish on chopsticks laid across a plate.
Bring the water in a steamer to a boil, put in the fish and steam over high heat for 10 minutes.
Move the fish to a clean plate and remove the ginger and scallion it was steamed with.
Pour the soy sauce over the fish and scatter the remaining ginger and the scallion greens on top.
Heat the oil in a small pan until very hot and pour it over the fish. Serve.

recipes.title: Wine-steamed Prawns
recipes.description: Prawns steamed on onion and ginger in rice wine, served with a hot soy, garlic and vinegar dip.

steps.instructionText: Cut the onion into small pieces and slice the ginger. Spread them over the base of a wide pan.
Rinse the prawns (deveining and trimming the legs is optional), drain and lay them on the onion and ginger.
Pour in the rice wine, cover and cook over medium heat for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to low and cook for 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes more.
Meanwhile, make the dip: chop the scallion and mince the garlic, then mix them with the soy sauce, sesame seeds and vinegar.
Heat the oil until hot and pour it over the dip.
Lift the prawns onto a clean plate and serve with the dip.

recipes.title: Steamed Pork Patty with Egg
recipes.description: Seasoned minced pork steamed on a plate with a whole egg in the centre.

steps.instructionText: In a bowl, mix the pork with the rice wine, soy sauce, white pepper, 1 of the eggs and the sesame oil until well combined.
Spread the pork over a plate. Make a hollow in the middle with a spoon and crack the other egg into it.
Fill a pot a quarter full with water and bring to a boil. Put in the plate, cover and steam for 15 minutes.
